compatibility_constraints.constraint: Legacy .claude/team.config.json remains honored below .omp precedence; existing consumer projects (pattern observed in herdr-omp-tg) keep working.
Project-local copied command files remain functional compatibility artifacts during migration to namespaced aliases; they never become an override API (REQ-15).
Existing shipped profiles (standard.json, spec-preparation.json) keep producing identical artifact chains; checkpoint-coverage additions are additive and versioned.
AGENT_MAPPING_SCHEMA carries a version; schema evolution invalidates older mapping files cleanly instead of misreading them.
Legacy pi.extensions manifest alias for omp.extensions continues to be accepted by the host contract relied upon here.
Historical non-namespaced invocations (/do-work, /team, /cto) keep working via canonical core registration while namespaced aliases are introduced alongside.

Without an explicitly activated SandboxGrant, workflow behavior is exactly the interactive final-DEC-1 semantics (immutable floor + profile checkpoints); no default, implicit, inherited, or config-implied unattended mode exists.

The unattended sandbox is additive and versioned: profiles/workflows without unattended declarations behave unchanged, and a consumer encountering an unsupported grant-schema version fails closed instead of approximating its meaning.

WorkDecompositionPlan schema and formula_version are versioned: encountering an unsupported formula_version or plan schema fails closed instead of approximating; profiles without dynamic-slice stages keep producing identical artifact chains (COMPAT-3/COMPAT-4 pattern).

D7-C state/report schemas are versioned and additive to existing durable artifacts; unsupported state/report versions, ambiguous authority, or non-atomic migration fail closed, while finalized reports remain readable with their run artifacts.

D3-A intentionally provides no compatibility alias, preset, or deprecation period for minimal/pragmatic/clean: old top-level, nested, and persisted values fail before planning as LEGACY_TIER_UNSUPPORTED; all other prior workflow contracts remain preserved.

Rubric/dimension schema and hashes are versioned; compatible namespaced bundle additions preserve core dimensions and old plan immutability, while unsupported, colliding, or drifted additions fail closed and require a new plan.

coverage_summary: P1-P6, evidence, contracts, SandboxGrant, DEC-1..DEC-2 and DEC-4..DEC-10 remain covered. TEN decisions are FINAL: DEC-1 D1-C, DEC-2 D2-C, DEC-3 D3-A, DEC-4 D4-C, DEC-5 D5-A, DEC-6, DEC-7 D7-C, DEC-8 D8-C, DEC-9 layered host+repo, DEC-10 D10-B. UDG-1..UDG-6 are resolved; no decision remains open. D7-C state/report authority, ring retention, redaction and resume recovery are covered by REQ-52..57 and related collections; D3-A cutover, core rubric, bundle ownership and hash binding by REQ-58..61 and related collections.

edge_cases.scenario: Ping storm: multiple parent or peer messages arrive during one long worker tool call
edge_cases.expected: All queued in order at the safe host queue/tool-call boundary, delivered at the next boundary; the active call completes untouched; zero synthetic skips, zero lost writes

edge_cases.scenario: Synthetic skip of a potentially non-idempotent operation under legacy replay path
edge_cases.expected: Replay at most once ONLY with trustworthy authoritative not_started proof from the dispatch id/state record (accepted|started|not_started|completed); absent or untrusted proof -> loud unrecoverable-skip error for manual resolution (no-proof-no-replay)

edge_cases.scenario: roster_overrides conflict with situational derivation (duplicate/opposing entries)
edge_cases.expected: Benign pins within the safety envelope win deterministically; an override violating pool membership, global(8)/per-role(3) caps, dependencies/disjointness, manual-QA/fan-in single-owner, or mandatory risk roles FAILS CLOSED with provenance instead of being applied; conflicts listed in diagnostics

edge_cases.scenario: Two plugins claim the same namespaced alias, or both claim canonical ownership
edge_cases.expected: Provider precedence picks per documented first-wins; loser receives diagnostic; unresolved CANONICAL ambiguity -> resolver rejection (FINAL DEC-4/D4-C: native/built-in/core precedence; load order is not API)

edge_cases.scenario: Capability pool filters to empty (all candidate agents unavailable)
edge_cases.expected: Explicit planning failure naming the starved role; never an empty dispatch or silent generic substitution

edge_cases.scenario: autonomous=true while a mandatory-human checkpoint class is reached
edge_cases.expected: Checkpoint stands; autonomy bypasses only non-mandatory classes (floor classes exactly per FINAL DEC-1/D1-C). In unattended mode the analogous encounter raises no ask: it defers per REQ-40

edge_cases.scenario: Both .omp and legacy .claude configs present and malformed
edge_cases.expected: Diagnostics for each file; defaults apply; precedence still reported by REQ-21 diagnostic

edge_cases.scenario: User hand-edits .work-state/runtime/agent-mapping.json
edge_cases.expected: Hash mismatch invalidates it; regeneration proceeds; user informed the edit was discarded

edge_cases.scenario: Worker finishes computation, then dies before the artifact write (exact incident shape)
edge_cases.expected: Recovery replays/resumes; artifact lands without recomputation; recovery provenance recorded

edge_cases.scenario: Correct-content artifact written at a non-contracted path
edge_cases.expected: Validation rejects with relocation guidance; slot remains incomplete until fixed (wrong-location class made actionable)

edge_cases.scenario: Parallel consilium slots persisting sibling artifacts concurrently
edge_cases.expected: Per-slot isolation (snapshotSlotArtifacts semantics); no cross-slot overwrite or merge

edge_cases.scenario: Bundle manifest declares engine version incompatible with installed core
edge_cases.expected: Fail closed at load with compatibility diagnostic (manifest remains descriptive-only per FINAL DEC-10/D10-B)

edge_cases.scenario: User changes active/default model expecting worker-model change
edge_cases.expected: Change applies to default model only; diagnostic explains @modelRoles and agent mapping are separate axes

edge_cases.scenario: Dispatch exits after consuming inputs but before writing its artifact (this run's recovery shape)
edge_cases.expected: Recovery continues the same stage instance from persisted context under an explicit no-new-research boundary

edge_cases.scenario: Ordinary parent status ping arrives while the worker holds an active tool call
edge_cases.expected: Ping queues at the safe boundary and is delivered afterwards (consolidated per stage); the active call is never interrupted or skipped; no cancellation follows from the ping itself

edge_cases.scenario: Pre-planned decomposition yields N mutually independent narrow research/development slices
edge_cases.expected: Up to N allowed agents launched concurrently within execution-time caps; per-slice owners declared pre-dispatch; results fan in with per-slice attribution

edge_cases.scenario: A proposed slice boundary falls inside an inherently sequential stage (manual-qa E2E scenario)
edge_cases.expected: Split rejected at planning review; stage stays whole under one sequential owner; non-split rationale recorded

edge_cases.scenario: Long worker computation phase; parent sends no messages; safe boundaries recur
edge_cases.expected: Worker self-emits concise IRC progress beacons at intervals; parent receives liveness/progress evidence without polling; beacons do not disturb the active call

edge_cases.scenario: Peer agent steers a sibling worker directly
edge_cases.expected: Same safe queue/tool-call boundary path and consolidation rules as parent-origin steering; execution-time capability policies still bind everything the receiving worker may act on

edge_cases.scenario: Unattended agent reaches a production-deploy/rollback-shaped action while a grant is valid
edge_cases.expected: Fail closed BEFORE execution; durable deferred record (class=production-effect); run continues with the next reachable slice; no ask raised, no execution

edge_cases.scenario: git push / package publish to a remote during the sandbox window
edge_cases.expected: Remote push/publish is out of scope by default: deferred with typed reason; local commits on the bound worktree continue uninterrupted

edge_cases.scenario: Grant expires or is revoked mid-run
edge_cases.expected: In-flight call completes; the next gated classification reverts to DEC-1 interactive semantics (checkpoint raised or refusal) or terminates per resume policy; zero post-boundary ask-free privileged actions

edge_cases.scenario: Resume attempted on a different worktree/session, or with changed config/inventory hashes
edge_cases.expected: Revalidation fails closed; remaining gated work deferred; typed mismatch names the grant id and the differing dimension

edge_cases.scenario: Fixture/seed reset of isolated dev data inside the sandbox
edge_cases.expected: Executes ask-free when the resource is declared resettable/isolated in the grant; undeclared or shared-state data is deferred instead

edge_cases.scenario: Every remaining slice blocked behind deferred actions (nothing reachable)
edge_cases.expected: Prompt terminal handoff enumerating deferred ids/classes/reasons; immediate termination; no polling loop

edge_cases.scenario: Ambiguous environment: dev and production domains indistinguishable from the runtime
edge_cases.expected: Fail closed and defer affected actions; the run never guesses a target's class

edge_cases.scenario: Orchestrator considers cancelling/restarting a live worker during an unattended run
edge_cases.expected: Cancel/restart of a possibly-computation-bearing worker is floor-gated: it is never executed ask-free; the DEC-6 recovery-first evidence ladder applies; restart WITHOUT a gate is permitted only for a dispatch proven not_started or failed with no computation loss (outside the cancellation class per final DEC-1)

edge_cases.scenario: Nested team spawns workers while the parent run already holds 7 of 8 global leases
edge_cases.expected: Nested requests draw the SAME central budget: admission up to 8, then typed queueing to the next wave; concurrency never transiently exceeds 8; per-role cap 3 enforced across parent+child combined

edge_cases.scenario: Ten independent slices ready, only 3 leases free
edge_cases.expected: 3 admitted in wave order (mandatory risk roles, then dependency-unblocking critical-path, phase order, slice_id); remaining 7 queued deterministically; each release admits the next candidate; none dropped

edge_cases.scenario: Identical inputs replayed, then one config hash changed
edge_cases.expected: Unchanged inputs reproduce the identical plan_hash and wave sequence; the changed input yields different plan identity with old-to-new provenance; the stale plan cannot launch

edge_cases.scenario: Override pins count=5 (per-role cap 3) or names an out-of-pool agent
edge_cases.expected: Fail closed at planning: override set rejected with provenance naming entry + violated constraint; derived plan stands; launch only after corrected overrides revalidate (new overrides hash -> new plan identity)

edge_cases.scenario: Inventory/config/mapping drift between plan creation and launch (stale plan)
edge_cases.expected: Launch refused naming drifted dimension(s); deterministic replanning emits a new versioned plan; provenance records both hash sets; in-flight slices finish under their launched plan untouched

edge_cases.scenario: Security specialist demanded but pool has none after the full fallback chain
edge_cases.expected: Compatible ordered fallback only; exhaustion on a mandatory capability yields typed unavailable naming slice_id/capability/tried candidates (unattended: durable deferral, run continues reachable slices); never silently merged into a generic role nor dropped

edge_cases.scenario: The 33rd invalidation/fallback event is appended
edge_cases.expected: CAS/atomic append stores the new monotonic event, evicts exactly the oldest ring entry, retains exactly the latest 32 in sequence, and never exposes a partial ring or alters the current snapshot

edge_cases.scenario: Report metadata/hash disagrees with authoritative state
edge_cases.expected: State remains authoritative; stale-projection diagnostic is emitted, the report is deterministically regenerated or finalization is refused, and logs are not consulted as truth

edge_cases.scenario: Resume finds no finalized report
edge_cases.expected: Valid authoritative state permits deterministic report regeneration and records recovery; missing/corrupt state fails closed and a report alone cannot resume the run

edge_cases.scenario: Resolver receives an outside-repository or malicious path
edge_cases.expected: Normalized repo-relative paths are accepted only inside the project; absolute/home/traversal paths are rejected or replaced by opaque stable ID/hash before state/report persistence

edge_cases.scenario: Legacy minimal/pragmatic/clean appears nested in input or in persisted state
edge_cases.expected: Planning never starts; resolver returns LEGACY_TIER_UNSUPPORTED with field/path and situational rubric guidance; no alias, mapping, ranking, or deprecation fallback occurs

edge_cases.scenario: Two bundles add the same rubric namespace or incompatible dimension
edge_cases.expected: Bundle validation fails closed before planning with both owners/namespaces and incompatibility details; core dimensions and safety remain unchanged

edge_cases.scenario: Rubric or namespaced dimension hash drifts after planning
edge_cases.expected: Launch/resume is refused as stale, drifted hashes are named, and deterministic replanning creates a new versioned plan; the old plan is immutable

error_behavior.condition: Malformed JSON in a team config file
error_behavior.behavior: parse-failure diagnostic (file + reason) emitted; built-in defaults apply; NEVER silent (changes current silent-catch)

error_behavior.condition: Generated mapping preferences_hash stale or hand-edited
error_behavior.behavior: mapping ignored + regenerated; info/warning diagnostic records invalidation cause

error_behavior.condition: Requested role has no resolvable agent in discovered inventory
error_behavior.behavior: explicit unavailable status on the role; stage plan degrades visibly or fails planning; no silent generic-agent swap

error_behavior.condition: Command/agent name collision at registration or discovery
error_behavior.behavior: challenger skipped; diagnostic lists owner, shadowed name, source path

error_behavior.condition: Advance attempted with unresolved checkpoint
error_behavior.behavior: blocking error naming the checkpoint and how to resolve (existing unresolvedCheckpointError semantics)

error_behavior.condition: Steering message lands during in-flight tool call (legacy skip path)
error_behavior.behavior: at-most-once transparent verbatim replay if the authoritative dispatch id/state record proves not_started; otherwise explicit unrecoverable-skip error naming dispatch id and observed state, escalated to manual resolution (no-proof-no-replay); the worker never silently loses the call

error_behavior.condition: Worker silent but state=Running within bounded window
error_behavior.behavior: no cancellation, no escalating pings (consolidation applies); orchestrator collects progress/lifecycle/recoverable evidence; intervention only on evidence failure or expiry of the agreed escalation bound per final DEC-6; recovery precedes any rerun

error_behavior.condition: Invalid or ambiguous bundle/profile selection
error_behavior.behavior: resolver error reporting effective source and provenance; no silent fallback to a different bundle

error_behavior.condition: Artifact produced at wrong location (content correct)
error_behavior.behavior: validation rejects by contract path; error suggests contracted location; slot counts as incomplete until relocated

error_behavior.condition: Replay candidate lacks trustworthy authoritative not_started proof (missing dispatch identity, or observed state started/completed/unknown)
error_behavior.behavior: NO replay; loud unrecoverable-skip error naming the dispatch id and observed state; manual resolution required (no-proof-no-replay)

error_behavior.condition: Floor-class or out-of-scope action attempted while a valid SandboxGrant is active
error_behavior.behavior: FAIL CLOSED: typed refusal, durable deferred_action record (class, reason, secrets redacted), immediate continuation with other reachable slices; a runtime ask/checkpoint is NEVER raised for such an action in unattended mode

error_behavior.condition: Environment cannot be proven at activation or mid-run (unknown/ambiguous host, worktree/branch/session mismatch, config/inventory hash mismatch, dev-vs-production indistinguishable)
error_behavior.behavior: fail closed and defer affected actions with a typed environment-proof reason; the zero-ask window does not open (activation) or closes (mid-run)

error_behavior.condition: Expired, revoked, or mismatched grant presented at start or resume
error_behavior.behavior: fail closed: zero ask-free privileged actions; typed diagnostic names grant id and failing dimension (expired/revoked/identity/hash); remaining gated work deferred; run downgrades to DEC-1 interactive semantics or terminates per REQ-44

error_behavior.condition: No reachable work remains while deferred actions pend
error_behavior.behavior: prompt terminal handoff enumerating deferred ids/classes/reasons and completed slices; no wait/poll/retry loop

error_behavior.condition: roster_overrides entry violates the safety envelope (out-of-pool agent, count above caps, broken dependency/disjointness, second manual-QA/fan-in owner)
error_behavior.behavior: ENTIRE override application rejected at planning (fail closed); typed conflict names formula_version, offending entry, violated constraint, derived-vs-pinned values; launch blocked until corrected; never clamped or partially applied

error_behavior.condition: Lease request exceeds the global(8)/per-role(3)/manual-QA(1) budget incl. nested-team requests
error_behavior.behavior: admission denied with typed cap reason; requester queued to the next wave in REQ-47 order; global budget never transiently exceeded; denials observable via REQ-27 session summaries

error_behavior.condition: Mutation of a launched WorkDecompositionPlan attempted, or launch attempted with drifted plan_hash
error_behavior.behavior: typed immutable-plan/stale-plan rejection naming drifted dimension(s); the launched version stays authoritative; corrected via deterministic replanning into a NEW versioned plan (REQ-6 checkpoint applies unless valid autonomous bypass)

error_behavior.condition: Mandatory slice capability unresolvable after compatible ordered fallback exhaustion
error_behavior.behavior: typed unavailable outcome naming slice_id, capability, tried candidates; interactive: visible degradation or planning failure; unattended: durable deferral and continuation on reachable slices; never silent substitution or silent drop

error_behavior.condition: Resolver state CAS conflict or non-atomic persistence
error_behavior.behavior: retry only against the current version or fail closed with a typed state-write error; no partial snapshot/ring/report is visible and the run cannot claim the write succeeded

error_behavior.condition: Report projection is stale, mismatched, or corrupt versus authoritative state
error_behavior.behavior: state remains authority; emit a typed stale-report diagnostic, regenerate deterministic projection when state is valid, and refuse finalization if consistency cannot be proven; logs never repair truth

error_behavior.condition: Finalized report is missing during resume
error_behavior.behavior: regenerate and reattach it from valid authoritative state with recovery provenance; if state is missing/corrupt, fail closed with typed resume-state error and do not trust report/log alone

error_behavior.condition: Forbidden secret, token, personal content, absolute/home/traversal, or outside-project path reaches a durability boundary
error_behavior.behavior: redaction rejects or replaces the value with opaque stable ID/hash before write; state/report publication fails closed with field-level diagnostic and no raw value persists

error_behavior.condition: Nested or persisted minimal/pragmatic/clean tier value encountered
error_behavior.behavior: planning is blocked before any option ranking with code LEGACY_TIER_UNSUPPORTED, offending field/path, and actionable core-rubric guidance; no alias, preset, silent mapping, or deprecation path

error_behavior.condition: Bundle rubric namespace collision or incompatible/core-overriding dimension declaration
error_behavior.behavior: fail closed before planning, naming bundle/namespace/dimension and conflict; no automatic rename, merge, reweight, shadow, or safety bypass

error_behavior.condition: Rubric/core/namespaced dimension hash drift at launch or resume
error_behavior.behavior: typed stale-plan/resume rejection names each drift; launched plan remains immutable and correction requires deterministic new versioned plan with old-to-new provenance

functional_requirements.statement: Workflow autonomy MUST be decided semantically by the orchestrating model under the model-first PHASE-0 contract; keyword heuristics MUST NOT set, backfill, or override the autonomous flag.
acceptance: Task text containing autonomy-suggesting keywords yields effective autonomous=false unless model classification independently returns autonomous=true.
Engine refuses to complete partial model classification from keywordClassify (existing refusal behavior preserved).

functional_requirements.statement: A leading autonomy directive parsed from task text MUST remain a NON-AUTHORITATIVE hint; autonomy MUST NOT be inferred from the command variant invoked (/do-work vs /team vs /cto) alone.
acceptance: Identical task text submitted via different command variants produces identical PHASE-0 autonomy evaluation.
Autonomy hint value alone never flips durable autonomous flag.

functional_requirements.statement: Every genuinely irreversible/destructive stage boundary in every shipped workflow profile MUST declare a checkpoint, and advancing past a stage with an unresolved checkpoint decision MUST remain blocked.
acceptance: Audit of shipped profiles (standard.json, spec-preparation.json) finds declared checkpoint at each boundary classified irreversible.
advanceCursor attempt unresolved declared checkpoint fails blocking error naming checkpoint.

functional_requirements.statement: Even under a validly granted autonomous mode, the FINAL DEC-1 immutable core floor stays human-checkpoint-gated and consists EXACTLY of: (1) production deploy/rollback; (2) destructive or irreversible git/filesystem/database/data/schema operations; (3) irreversible external publish/send/payment/account effects; (4) credential/access/security-policy changes; (5) cancellation/restart of a live worker whose computation may be lost - while a dispatch proven not_started, or failed with no loss of computation, is OUTSIDE the cancellation class. Profiles MAY add contextual checkpoints on top; neither the model, hints, command variants, nor task text can remove, weaken, or self-approve any floor class.
source: U:continuation feedback (UDG-3 final: DEC-1 D1-C with exact immutable floor classes)
acceptance: Each of five floor classes raises human checkpoint in ordinary-autonomy mode; attempting one raises checkpoint instead of proceeding.
Profile-added checkpoints block identically; no input channel (model output, hint, command variant, task text) can resolve or delete floor or profile checkpoint.
A proven-not_started or failed-with-no-computation-loss dispatch restarts without floor checkpoint, per REQ-29 semantics.
In unattended mode same five classes never auto-execute: they defer per REQ-40.

functional_requirements.statement: CTO MUST remain a main-session orchestration boundary (never dispatched as an ordinary task-agent worker) with human-in-the-loop escalation semantics for irreversible or ambiguous decisions.
acceptance: CTO invocable in main session; attempts to spawn cto as Task worker rejected by roster policy.
Escalation flows through escalation-adapter channel and waits for human answer before irreversible steps.

functional_requirements.statement: Dynamic roster/planning outcomes MUST be presented as a proposed plan gated by a checkpoint before any dispatch, unless autonomy was explicitly and validly requested under REQ-1/REQ-4 semantics.
acceptance: With autonomous=false, roster-changing plan pauses at recorded checkpoint before first dispatch.
With valid explicit autonomous grant, dispatch proceeds and grant provenance recorded in durable state.

functional_requirements.statement: The allowed roster MUST be treated as a capability pool: discovery output is INPUT to planning only; permission MUST be enforced at execution time (parent spawn policy, disabledAgents, recursion depth, exact agent lookup).
acceptance: An agent absent from discovered inventory never dispatched regardless of planner output.
task.disabledAgents / recursion-depth policies still reject requested agents at execution time.

functional_requirements.statement: Slot multiplicity and composition MUST derive situationally from project shape/composition signals (e.g., module count, changed-surface size) instead of a fixed per-stage role list; roster_overrides remain the deterministic manual trim on top.
acceptance: The same profile applied to repositories differing in chosen shape signals resolves to different slot sets, deterministically per inputs.
roster_overrides applied after situational derivation always produce overridden result (manual trim wins deterministically).

functional_requirements.statement: Role resolution MUST use ordered fallback chains (role -> candidate agents) resolved against live discovered inventory, and an unresolvable role MUST degrade EXPLICITLY (status preferred|fallback|unavailable surfaced), never by silent generic substitution.
acceptance: Every effective role->agent assignment reports its resolution status and reason for any fallback.
A role no resolvable candidate yields explicit unavailable outcome visible to orchestrator.

functional_requirements.statement: Dynamic roster planning MUST produce a structured proposed-roster artifact (selected subset, per-role justification, fallback decisions) BEFORE task dispatch, linked to the REQ-6 checkpoint when autonomy does not bypass it.
acceptance: For every dynamically-sized stage, proposed-roster artifact exists prior to first dispatch and matches what was actually dispatched (or recorded override).

functional_requirements.statement: Dispatch MUST NOT launch every discovered role by default; the default is the selected justified subset for the stage's needs.
acceptance: Adding unrelated agent to environment does not change any stage's dispatched set in absence of matching stage needs.

functional_requirements.statement: Architecture option formation MUST be situational: the consilium evaluates concrete context and ranks options with explicit rationale using the mandatory core rubric (scope,risk,reversibility,uncertainty,coupling,blast_radius,cost,evidence_quality), never hard-coded quality tiers.
acceptance: An options_decision_log evaluates each option against all eight core dimensions, states deterministic aggregation semantics, and records explicit context-fit rationale/tradeoffs.
minimal, pragmatic, and clean absent from required config/input/schema/output/state/docs/tests; no tier value can select, rank, or promote option.

functional_requirements.statement: Recommendations in research/consilium artifacts MUST remain provisional until the designated decision stage; after a logged decision, only that explicit decision and rationale may become authoritative, never a fixed-tier alias, preset, or silent promotion.
acceptance: Downstream artifacts mark options provisional until decision-log entry exists.
After entry, selected option carries logged rationale and no legacy tier vocabulary emitted.

functional_requirements.statement: Bundle-specific workflow commands MUST be registered under an explicit bundle namespace (sole registered grammar: host-verified hyphen aliases do-work-<bundle>, team-<bundle>, cto-<bundle>; colon grammar unverified and not API); independently loaded extensions MUST NOT assume same-name ownership because programmatic extension command names are global and collision-sensitive.
acceptance: Registering second plugin claiming already-owned name results in challenger being skipped WITH diagnostic naming owner and source.
Namespaced aliases coexist canonical commands without shadowing them.

functional_requirements.statement: Core retains canonical ownership of /do-work, /team, /cto registration; project-local copied command files remain compatibility artifacts and MUST NOT act as an override API.
acceptance: Editing copied project-local command file does not alter effective command behavior of canonical registration.
Canonical commands resolve to core registration under documented provider precedence.

functional_requirements.statement: Bundle contract: core owns engine/templates/contracts; each bundle owns a NAMESPACED role catalog, agent definitions, fallback chains, scope defaults, and optional canonical command aliases, exposed via a versioned manifest including engine compatibility metadata.
acceptance: A bundle whose manifest declares incompatible engine versions fails closed diagnostic instead of loading.
Role catalog keys namespaced at config layer while resolving to actual global agent names at dispatch.

functional_requirements.statement: Name precedence MUST be explicit and diagnosable: per FINAL DEC-4 (D4-C) the documented native/built-in/core precedence stands, every challenger claim is diagnosed with owner/source/precedence and accepted-or-rejected result, ambiguous CANONICAL ownership is strictly REJECTED rather than silently picked, and arbitrary plugin load order is never treated as an ownership API; team-config precedence remains .omp/team.config.json > legacy .claude/team.config.json > built-in defaults.
source: U:continuation feedback (UDG-2 final folded per NF-12)
acceptance: Every effective command/agent name resolution can be explained from diagnostic report (owner + source path).
Ambiguous dual ownership produces resolver error or diagnostic, never silent winner.

functional_requirements.statement: Agent identity, semantic role, and model role MUST be kept distinct in user-facing config schema, documentation, and error messages (changing active/default model does not remap @modelRoles; changing roles remaps agent selection).
acceptance: Changing active model triggers diagnostic clarifying that custom model roles unaffected.
Error messages about mapping failures name which of identity/role/model-role was involved.

functional_requirements.statement: Config and mapping resolution MUST emit diagnostics for every failure mode (malformed JSON, missing file, unexpected location, stale preferences_hash, unavailable-agent fallback); silent catch-and-default behavior MUST be removed from resolveConfig(), loadTeamConfig(), and writeConfig() paths.
acceptance: Feeding malformed JSON yields diagnostic naming file and parse offset, then defaults apply.
No code path swallows config parse/write error without emitting diagnostic.

functional_requirements.statement: There MUST be exactly ONE shared team-config resolution path used by both the engine and command entrypoints; the divergent duplicate reader in do-work (roles-only) MUST be eliminated or rerouted through the shared resolver.
acceptance: A change in team config affects engine dispatch and command-layer rendering identically in same run.
Grep-level audit finds single config-read implementation referenced by both layers.

functional_requirements.statement: An effective-configuration diagnostic MUST expose, per resolution: actual config sources, bundle/profile, role catalog, mapping preferences_hash, inventory, effective role->agent mapping/status, and fallback reasons; the ONE shared resolver MUST write these facts to authoritative compact per-run resume state and a deterministic human-readable report, while logs remain telemetry only.
acceptance: A config-ignored report identifies stale hash, fallback, cwd/config root, or model-role conflation and distinguishes file-not-found, parse-error, and hash-stale.
The same resolution appears in authoritative state and report; changing/truncating logs cannot change resume truth.

functional_requirements.statement: Stale generated mappings MUST self-invalidate on preferences_hash mismatch and regenerate; invalidation, discarded hand-edits, and fallback provenance MUST be recorded in authoritative state/report, never applied silently.
acceptance: Hand-editing agent-mapping triggers regeneration plus discarded-edit diagnostic.
The invalidation/fallback event durably retained and projected in finalized report; logs alone insufficient.

functional_requirements.statement: A specialized development bundle/command for building THIS plugin MUST package the recurring moves: release-readiness checks (release-preflight precedent), scoped package validation, session-history queries (the ad-hoc grep/python of the intake scan), and work-state-aware dispatch.
acceptance: Invoking dev command executes readiness checks, scoped validation, and history queries without manual step reconstruction.
Command/agents follow REQ-14 namespace rule.

functional_requirements.statement: Every subagent restart/interruption MUST be attributable to one declared cause class: (a) engine REJECTED validation, (b) worker completed without declared-artifact evidence, (c) coordination-layer steering skip/starvation, (d) ambiguous instructions/scope drift. Cause class MUST be observable post-hoc.
acceptance: For any aborted/restarted stage instance in session logs, dominant cause class derivable from recorded events without guesswork.
Class (c) occurrences distinguishable from (a) by absence of any REJECTED code and presence of synthetic-skip markers.

functional_requirements.statement: Computed-but-unpersisted deliverables MUST be recoverable: a worker interrupted after finishing computation but before/at the artifact write MUST be resumable (verbatim replay of the lost write, or resume from durable snapshot/transcript) WITHOUT recomputing the underlying research.
acceptance: Replaying incident timeline ends artifact written and zero recomputation of prior tool work.
Recovery provenance (what was restored vs re-derived) recorded in recovered artifact.

functional_requirements.statement: Stage completion MUST require the declared artifact at its contracted path, validated by contract (validateProduced / validateProducedMultiSlot); content-correct artifacts at wrong locations count as NOT completed for that slot and receive relocation guidance.
acceptance: A slot reporting done without its declared artifact fails stage gate missing-artifact error naming expected path.
An artifact found at non-contracted path yields validation error suggesting contracted location.

functional_requirements.statement: Session observability: WORKFLOW_* state transitions per session MUST be exposed in a structured, greppable summary (small query helper), making restart-cause frequency measurable instead of reconstructed.
acceptance: Per-session and per-project counts of each WORKFLOW_* code (incl. *_REJECTED) queryable in one command.
Lost historical numbers remain marked lost until re-measured by this helper; no fabricated statistics enter decisions.

functional_requirements.statement: Parent-to-worker AND peer-to-peer steering messages MUST be delivered as QUEUED DATA at the next tool-call boundary through the SAFE HOST QUEUE/TOOL-CALL BOUNDARY, never by aborting the worker's in-flight interruptible wait (clean design, PX-1). Per final DEC-9 the implementation locus is LAYERED HOST+REPO: the host supplies the safe queue/tool-call boundary together with the authoritative dispatch id/state record; the repository consumes these primitives and implements recovery-first fallbacks on top.
source: U:continuation feedback (DEC-9 final: layered host+repo; parent/peer steering via safe host queue/tool-call boundary)
acceptance: Replaying incident ping pattern against improved system produces zero skipped tool calls and zero lost writes.
Message ordering preserved; worker observes messages at natural pause.
A peer-origin steering message traverses same queue/boundary path and consolidation rules as parent-origin one.

functional_requirements.statement: Mechanical floor for legacy synthetic-skip systems: IF a harness version still synthesizes a skip for an in-flight call, the call MAY be replayed verbatim AT MOST ONCE automatically once the steering queue drains, and ONLY when the AUTHORITATIVE DISPATCH ID/STATE record proves not_started (state vocabulary: accepted | started | not_started | completed). This is no-proof-no-replay: absent, ambiguous, or untrustworthy proof MUST fail loudly to manual resolution instead of ever executing the call twice.
source: U:continuation feedback (DEC-9 final: authoritative dispatch id/state accepted|started|not_started|completed; guarded single replay only with trustworthy not_started proof; no-proof-no-replay)

functional_requirements.statement: State-aware recovery-first orchestration policy (FINAL per DEC-6): a 'Still Running' lifecycle state and temporary artifact absence MUST NOT be treated as hang signals and MUST NOT hang the orchestrator; ordinary parent pings MUST NOT interrupt or abort a worker's active tool calls; before any cancellation the orchestrator MUST collect progress/lifecycle/recoverable evidence; cancellation is permitted ONLY on evidence failure (work provably lost/worker dead) or an agreed escalation bound; recovery precedes rerun (repo recovery-first). Steering to a live worker remains consolidated (prefer one message per stage); ladder: wait -> single consolidated ping -> bounded timeout -> only then intervention.
source: U:user_feedback_binding (Still Running != hang; cancellation was wrong)
acceptance: A worker mid-tool-call no artifact on disk yet never cancelled solely due to elapsed time inside bounded window.
Multiple status requests arriving during one stage collapse into at most one delivered ping.
Every cancel decision references either recorded evidence failure or configured/agreed escalation bound; neither present, no cancellation occurs.

functional_requirements.statement: An escape hatch for TRUE urgent aborts MUST survive any queuing design: dedicated abort signaling bypasses the queue and takes effect promptly.
source: U:continuation feedback (DEC-9 final retains explicit abort bypass)

functional_requirements.statement: Recovery after a failed/interrupted dispatch MUST continue the SAME stage instance from persisted context (durable state, snapshots, transcript-derived findings) with an explicit no-new-wide-research boundary, rather than restarting the stage from scratch.

functional_requirements.statement: The planner/orchestrator MUST decompose research and development work IN ADVANCE into NARROW SLICES with exactly ONE CLEAR OWNER each, declaring slice boundaries, ownership, and expected outputs in the pre-dispatch planning/proposed-roster artifact (linked to REQ-10).
source: U:continuation feedback (planner/orchestrator pre-splits research/development into narrow clear-ownership slices)
acceptance: Every dispatched research/development task names exactly one owning agent and bounded deliverable; shared-ownership slices fail planning review.

functional_requirements.statement: Launched agent count MUST follow independent decomposition: the orchestrator launches AS MANY ALLOWED AGENTS as the independent slices require (within execution-time roster/policy caps) rather than a fixed per-stage number; PEER-TO-PEER IRC COLLABORATION and FAN-IN of partial results across concurrently running peers are permitted and attributed.

functional_requirements.statement: Inherently sequential stages (canonical exemplar: manual-qa end-to-end scenario execution) MUST remain WHOLE under a SINGLE SEQUENTIAL OWNER who executes the scenario in order; they MUST NOT be mechanically split across parallel agents merely to satisfy slicing/parallelism rules; the plan records the non-split rationale instead.

functional_requirements.statement: Workers MUST SELF-INITIATE CONCISE PROGRESS BEACONS via IRC at SAFE BOUNDARIES (between tool calls) at regular intervals, each carrying dispatch/stage identity, current state (using the accepted|started|not_started|completed vocabulary where applicable), and the next step. Beacons are fire-and-forget observability: emission MUST NOT interrupt the worker's own active call, and parents obtain progress WITHOUT issuing status requests (ordinary polling pings remain unnecessary and never preempt active calls per REQ-28/REQ-30).
source: U:continuation feedback (workers periodically send concise progress beacons via IRC at safe boundaries, without interrupting parent status requests)

Beacon emission leaves active tool calls untouched (no skip/replay side effects) and preserves INV-6.
Beacon absence consumed as INPUT to DEC-6 evidence ladder (LC-11), never as immediate interrupt/cancel trigger.

functional_requirements.statement: Unattended ('night') operation MUST be OPT-IN via EXPLICIT ACTIVATION that creates a durable, scoped SANDBOX GRANT. The grant MUST record: a unique grant id; activator identity/provenance; the bound branch/worktree/session identity; the allowed dev targets, resources, and action classes; an explicit forbidden-action list; a hard expiry; config/inventory hashes pinning the environment; and a resume policy. Absent a valid grant the workflow behaves exactly as the interactive modes defined by final DEC-1 (immutable floor + profile checkpoints).

functional_requirements.statement: While a valid SandboxGrant is active, the run MUST present ZERO runtime asks/checkpoints: ordinary confirmations inside the granted scope proceed without asking, and no engine checkpoint blocks in-scope stage advance. Floor-class actions (final DEC-1) and out-of-scope actions likewise raise NO runtime ask - they FAIL CLOSED into durable deferred_actions/handoff per REQ-40. The coordination policy (REQ-28 queuing, REQ-30 recovery-first ladder, REQ-36 beacons) remains fully in force inside the window.

Beacon emission and queued steering behave exactly as in interactive mode throughout window.

Deferred records survive interruption and appear in both resumed run state and terminal handoff.

functional_requirements.statement: Every unattended classification MUST be made against a PROVEN environment: the runtime MUST demonstrate that branch, worktree, session identity, and config/inventory hashes match the grant record. An UNKNOWN or AMBIGUOUS environment - including any inability to reliably distinguish a dev target from a production one - FAILS CLOSED and defers the affected action.

functional_requirements.statement: Resuming an interrupted unattended run MUST revalidate BOTH the grant (grant id, not expired, not revoked, config/inventory hashes intact) AND the target identity (branch/worktree/session identity) according to the grant's resume policy BEFORE any ask-free continuation; ANY mismatch fails closed, defers remaining gated work, and downgrades the run to final DEC-1 interactive semantics.

functional_requirements.statement: A SandboxGrant MUST carry a HARD EXPIRY and MUST support explicit REVOCATION. On expiry or revocation the zero-ask window closes: the in-flight tool call is allowed to finish (never killed mid-call, preserving INV-10), and every subsequent gated classification reverts to final DEC-1 interactive semantics (checkpoint raised or action refused).

functional_requirements.statement: When an unattended run reaches a state with NO REACHABLE SLICE left (all remaining work deferred, blocked, or out of scope), it MUST terminate promptly with a durable HANDOFF summarizing completed slices, open deferred actions (ids/classes/reasons), and grant/environment status. Idling, polling, sleep-retry loops, and synthetic activity are prohibited.

acceptance: The terminal state contains handoff artifact enumerating every deferred action id recorded during run.
No polling/waiting pattern observable between last reachable action and termination.
Completed-slice summaries in handoff match validated stage-gate evidence (REQ-26), not claims.

functional_requirements.statement: Dynamic roster planning MUST emit a VERSIONED WorkDecompositionPlan BEFORE any dispatch (generalizing the REQ-10 proposed-roster artifact): a slice graph of narrow TYPED slices, pairwise DISJOINT (no shared ownership) and CLOSED (every dependency resolves to a declared slice_id or an external completed gate); each node declares stable slice_id, type, required capabilities, dependencies, IO contracts, EXACTLY ONE fan-in output owner, and evidence fields (REQ-46); the plan binds plan_hash over its six identity hashes (REQ-51).

functional_requirements.statement: Composition signals (risk, platform, package boundaries, public-API surface, data/migration footprint, infrastructure, security) MAY justify SEPARATE SLICES or SPECIALIST roles but MUST NEVER act as direct slot multipliers; the ONLY permitted quantitative sizing evidence is recoverable FILE COUNTS; token estimates and time budgets are FORBIDDEN sizing inputs.

File-count evidence cites path/glob reviewer can recompute.

functional_requirements.statement: Staffing assigns ONE CANDIDATE per SIMULTANEOUSLY READY INDEPENDENT slice, role multiplicity derived ONLY from ready-slice capabilities; excess ready slices form DETERMINISTIC LATER WAVES ordered: mandatory risk-role coverage FIRST, then dependency-unblocking critical-path priority, then phase order, then stable slice_id; NO ready slice is dropped.

Admitted + queued always equal planned slices.

functional_requirements.statement: Concurrency is governed by CENTRAL LEASES: GLOBAL CAP 8 running worker leases across the ENTIRE workflow run INCLUDING nested teams, PER-ROLE CAP 3, MANUAL-QA ONE WHOLE sequential owner (REQ-35), EXACTLY ONE owner per fan-in output; leases are acquired before dispatch, released at terminal worker state; nested-team requests draw from the SAME budget.

functional_requirements.statement: Slice staffing uses COMPATIBLE ORDERED FALLBACK CHAINS ONLY (REQ-9): when a MANDATORY capability has no resolvable candidate after chain exhaustion, the outcome is TYPED UNAVAILABLE - visible degradation or planning failure interactively, durable DEFERRAL unattended (REQ-40) - never silent generic substitution, capability-less dispatch, or silent slice drop.

Unattended mode defers durably and continues reachable slices (never waits/polls).
Optional capabilities degrade surfaced preferred|fallback|unavailable status without blocking slice.

functional_requirements.statement: roster_overrides apply LAST after deterministic derivation and MAY pin min/max/count ONLY within: allowed discovered pool, global(8)/per-role(3) caps, dependencies/disjointness, manual-QA single whole owner, fan-in single-owner, mandatory risk-role coverage; ANY violating override FAILS CLOSED with provenance (formula_version, offending entry, violated constraint, derived-vs-pinned values) - never clamped silently or partially applied.

Provenance records derived value, pinned value, violated rule.

functional_requirements.statement: The WorkDecompositionPlan carries plan IDENTITY = formula_version + overrides + inventory + config + selection + mapping hashes; LAUNCH IS REFUSED on drift between planned and current hashes (stale invalidation); post-launch mutation is REJECTED - changed inputs force a NEW versioned plan via DETERMINISTIC REPLANNING under the REQ-6 gate, never an in-place edit.

acceptance: Recomputing six hashes at launch reproduces plan_hash; mismatch refuses launch naming drifted dimension(s).
Mutating launched plan returns typed immutable-plan error; launched version stays authoritative.
Replanning unchanged inputs yields identical successor; changed inputs yield different identity old-to-new provenance.

functional_requirements.statement: The ONE shared resolver MUST write an authoritative compact per-run resume state and a deterministic human-readable report from each resolution; logs may carry telemetry only and MUST NOT be an authority for planning or resume.
acceptance: Engine and command entrypoints produce one state snapshot and one report projection from the same resolver result.
A missing, truncated, or altered log cannot change the state used for resume; state/report writes are CAS/atomic and never expose a mixed result.

functional_requirements.statement: Per-run resume state MUST contain exactly one current effective snapshot and a monotonic ring of the latest 32 invalidation/fallback events; appending event 33 atomically evicts the oldest event, and the finalized report remains with the run artifacts.
acceptance: The snapshot is singular and current; event sequence numbers strictly increase and ring length is never above 32.
After 33 valid events the ring contains events 2..33 in order, with event 1 atomically gone and no partial ring.
Finalized report retention is independent of telemetry/state cleanup and remains addressable by run artifact identity.

functional_requirements.statement: The effective snapshot and event records MUST cover source, effective_config, manifest, catalog, inventory, selection, mapping, fallback, and invalidation fields; paths are normalized repo-relative and all other references use stable IDs or hashes sufficient to diagnose provenance.
acceptance: A state/report fixture contains every named field and identifies source-to-effective mapping, inventory, fallback, and invalidation reason.
Equivalent inputs produce byte-identical normalized identifiers and event ordering; outside-project sources are represented only by opaque stable ID/hash.

functional_requirements.statement: The human-readable report MUST be a deterministic projection of accepted authoritative state, include snapshot identity and event sequence/hash, explain staleness/fallback/invalidation, and become immutable when finalized with the run artifacts.
acceptance: Repeated projection of unchanged state is byte-identical and readable without telemetry access.
Finalization records the state projection hash; a later state change yields a new run/state version rather than mutating the finalized report.

functional_requirements.statement: Resume MUST recover from authoritative per-run state, validate the report projection against its state/version/hash, and treat a missing or stale report as recoverable projection work; a missing or corrupt authoritative state fails closed rather than trusting logs or a report alone.
acceptance: Resume with valid state and missing report deterministically regenerates and reattaches the report, recording the recovery event.
State/report mismatch is diagnosed as stale projection and never silently merged; no state means typed recovery failure and no speculative resume.

functional_requirements.statement: All durable resolver state, reports, and invalidation events MUST apply strict redaction: permit normalized repo-relative paths, stable IDs, and hashes; forbid absolute/home paths, traversal leakage, plaintext capability/dispatch/advance tokens, secrets/credential values, raw args, unrelated prompts, and personal content; outside-project sources become opaque stable ID/hash.
acceptance: A redaction audit rejects each forbidden value before any state or artifact write.
A path outside the project or containing traversal is replaced by an opaque stable identifier/hash; allowed repo-relative paths are normalized.

functional_requirements.statement: DEC-3 D3-A is a clean cutover: minimal, pragmatic, and clean MUST be removed from configuration/input schema, output, state, docs, and tests with no alias, preset, mapping, ranking, or deprecation period; any nested or persisted legacy tier value MUST fail before planning as LEGACY_TIER_UNSUPPORTED with actionable situational-field guidance and MUST NEVER be silently mapped or ranked.
acceptance: A top-level, nested, and persisted legacy value all stop before planning with code LEGACY_TIER_UNSUPPORTED and identify the offending field/path plus core rubric guidance.
No accepted input/output/state/config contains a legacy tier, alias, preset, or deprecation marker.

functional_requirements.statement: Core owns a mandatory, non-overridable rubric with exactly these dimensions: scope, risk, reversibility, uncertainty, coupling, blast_radius, cost, evidence_quality; every dimension has declared scale/direction and participates in versioned deterministic aggregation with explicit rationale, and core safety/checkpoint rules cannot be changed by a rubric value.
acceptance: A core rubric record contains all eight dimensions, scale/direction, aggregation semantics/version, and rationale; omission or duplicate core dimensions fails validation.
Changing a core dimension name, meaning, weight, scale, direction, or safety interpretation is rejected rather than accepted as a bundle override.

functional_requirements.statement: A bundle MAY add only versioned namespaced rubric dimensions; each addition MUST declare schema, scale, direction, evidence requirements, and dimension hash, and MUST NOT remove, rename, redefine, reweight, shadow, bypass, or weaken any core dimension or safety rule; namespace collision or incompatibility fails closed.
acceptance: A compatible bundle addition is isolated under its namespace and appears with its declared metadata/evidence/hash.
A collision or any attempted core modification produces a typed failure before planning; no automatic rename, merge, or fallback changes semantics.

functional_requirements.statement: Rubric, core-dimension, and accepted namespaced-dimension hashes MUST bind WorkDecompositionPlan identity and resume validity; hash drift is stale invalidation requiring refusal or deterministic replanning, never an in-place plan or resume mutation.
acceptance: Plan identity records rubric/dimension hashes and launch/resume recomputation names every drifted hash.
A changed core or bundle dimension hash refuses stale launch/resume and produces a new versioned plan with old-to-new provenance.

invariants.statement: No cursor advance past a stage with an unresolved declared checkpoint decision.
Every dispatch is authorized by an opaque capability; capability/dispatch/advance secrets exist only sha256-hashed at rest.
Roster discovery output is capability input, never permission; execution-time policies remain the sole authority on what may run.
Generated agent_mapping is accepted only when its preferences_hash matches current roles+extraRoles; stale mappings self-invalidate.
Keyword classification never decides autonomy; the model-first PHASE-0 contract is authoritative.
Coordination traffic (steering/pings) never destroys a worker's computed work; a computed deliverable is always recoverable or replayable.
At most one owner per command/agent name per discovery scope; any ambiguity is surfaced as a diagnostic, never silently resolved.
Subagents never invoke workflow_* control tools and never mutate canonical .work-state outside their owned artifacts; control remains main-session-only.
Unrecoverable evidence stays marked lost/unquantified; no statistic enters a decision without recoverable provenance.

Ordinary parent- or peer-origin coordination traffic is queued data delivered at the safe host queue/tool-call boundary; it never aborts, synthetic-skips, or preempts an in-flight tool call; only a dedicated urgent-abort signal bypasses the queue.

An automatic replay of a coordination-skipped call happens AT MOST ONCE and ONLY with trustworthy authoritative proof of not_started dispatch state (accepted|started|not_started|completed vocabulary); absent such proof the system fails loudly instead of replaying (no-proof-no-replay).
Cancellation of a running worker requires recorded evidence failure or an agreed escalation bound; 'Still Running' state or temporary artifact absence alone never justifies cancellation.
Every research/development slice has exactly one clear owner; inherently sequential stages (e.g., manual-qa) remain whole and are never mechanically split across agents.

A SandboxGrant removes zero-ask friction only INSIDE its declared scope and never touches the DEC-1 floor: floor-class actions are never auto-approved in unattended mode (they fail closed and defer); grant scope, targets, and resources are interpreted exactly as written; and pre-existing dev credentials/test accounts found in the environment confer no authority beyond the grant.

Every deferred action is durably recorded (deferred_actions/handoff) BEFORE the run continues; deferral never silently drops, retries, or executes the action, and deferred records always surface in resumes and the terminal handoff.

Unattended runs never block on, poll, or wait for human input: gated outcomes become durable deferrals, execution continues on reachable slices, and no-reachable-work ends in prompt termination with handoff.

Grant-boundary integrity: activation, in-run classification, and resume all validate environment proof (branch/worktree/session identity, config/inventory hashes) against the grant record; unknown or ambiguous environments fail closed.

Live worker leases never exceed 8 run-wide including nested-team descendants, 3 per role, and 1 whole sequential manual-QA owner; each fan-in output has exactly one owner; caps enforced by refusing admission with typed queueing (REQ-47 order), never warned after the fact.

Sizing derives exclusively from the WorkDecompositionPlan slice graph: risk/platform/package/public-API/data/migration/infra/security signals influence only slice boundaries/specialists, never slot arithmetic; quantitative sizing evidence limited to recoverable file counts; token/time estimates forbidden.

Wave formation and admission order are a pure function of (plan identity, readiness, priorities): mandatory risk roles first, then dependency-unblocking critical-path priority, then phase order, then stable slice_id; no ready slice dropped; identical inputs reproduce identical waves.

Overrides apply last strictly within the safety envelope (discovered pool, 8/3 caps, dependencies/disjointness, manual-QA/fan-in single-owner, mandatory risk roles); conflicts fail closed with provenance; a launched plan is immutable - mutation rejected, changes require a new versioned plan.

The shared resolver is the sole authority for per-run provenance: state and finalized report derive from one accepted result; logs are telemetry and cannot authorize planning, invalidate state, or resume.
Each run has one current effective snapshot and a monotonic invalidation/fallback ring capped at 32; every append and oldest-entry eviction is atomic/CAS and no partial state is observable.
A report is a deterministic, hash-bound projection of authoritative state; finalization is immutable, and state/report mismatch is stale projection rather than a second authority.

No durable resolver state/report contains forbidden tokens, secrets, credentials, raw args, unrelated prompts/personal content, absolute/home/traversal paths, or unopaque outside-project sources; redaction precedes every durability boundary.

The clean-cutover legacy tier vocabulary is absent from accepted surfaces; any nested or persisted minimal/pragmatic/clean value fails before planning as LEGACY_TIER_UNSUPPORTED and is never mapped or ranked.

Core owns all eight rubric dimensions and safety semantics; bundle additions are versioned and namespaced with declared schema/scale/direction/evidence/hash and cannot alter core; collisions/incompatibility fail closed.
Rubric and dimension hashes are part of plan identity and resume validity; drift refuses stale launch/resume and requires a new immutable versioned plan.

lifecycle_transitions.guarantee: zero lost in-flight work (INV-6); ordering preserved; authoritative dispatch id/state progresses accepted -> started -> completed

lifecycle_transitions.trigger: explicit activation request; grant fields complete; environment proof matches (branch/worktree/session, config/inventory hashes)
lifecycle_transitions.guarantee: durable versioned SandboxGrant stored with expiry/resume policy; window opens only after full validation; absent/invalid grant keeps exact DEC-1 interactive behavior

lifecycle_transitions.target: fail closed: typed refusal, durable deferred_action record (class, reason, redacted context), run continues with next reachable slice
lifecycle_transitions.guarantee: no runtime ask raised; floor never auto-executed (INV-14); continuation observed rather than stall

lifecycle_transitions.transition: window open -> grant expires or is revoked
lifecycle_transitions.trigger: expiry instant reached or explicit revoke operation
lifecycle_transitions.guarantee: in-flight tool call completes untouched (INV-10); subsequent gated classifications revert to DEC-1 interactive semantics; zero post-boundary ask-free privileged actions

lifecycle_transitions.trigger: resume per grant resume policy
lifecycle_transitions.guarantee: grant validity AND target identity revalidated (REQ-42); match continues ask-free; any mismatch fails closed, defers remaining gated work, downgrades to interactive semantics

lifecycle_transitions.transition: no reachable slice remains -> terminal handoff
lifecycle_transitions.trigger: all remaining work deferred/blocked/out-of-scope
lifecycle_transitions.guarantee: prompt termination with durable handoff enumerating deferred ids/classes/reasons and completed slices; no polling/idling

lifecycle_transitions.trigger: planning gate satisfied; slice graph validated (typed/disjoint/closed/single fan-in owners); plan_hash computed
lifecycle_transitions.guarantee: versioned WorkDecompositionPlan persisted pre-dispatch (REQ-45); REQ-6 checkpoint honored unless valid autonomous bypass; hash drift refuses launch (REQ-51)

lifecycle_transitions.transition: leases saturated -> excess ready slices queued -> released leases admit next candidates
lifecycle_transitions.trigger: live leases reach global/per-role/manual-QA cap while further slices become ready
lifecycle_transitions.guarantee: excess forms the deterministic next wave (mandatory risk roles, then dependency-unblocking critical-path, phase order, stable slice_id); none dropped; releases admit strictly in wave order; caps never transiently exceeded

lifecycle_transitions.transition: input drift -> stale invalidation -> deterministic replanning
lifecycle_transitions.trigger: inventory/config/overrides/mapping/selection hash mismatch versus the launched plan, detected pre-launch or mid-run
lifecycle_transitions.guarantee: launch refused or a NEW versioned plan created via deterministic replanning with old-to-new provenance; no in-place mutation; in-flight workers finish under their launched plan

lifecycle_transitions.transition: resolver result accepted -> state/report CAS write
lifecycle_transitions.trigger: one shared resolution completes with normalized provenance
lifecycle_transitions.guarantee: one atomic version publishes current snapshot, ring append, and report projection or publishes none; telemetry is non-authoritative

lifecycle_transitions.trigger: a new event arrives after the bounded ring is full
lifecycle_transitions.guarantee: monotonic event 33 is committed and oldest event 1 is atomically evicted; exactly 32 latest events remain

lifecycle_transitions.transition: run state finalized -> report artifact retained
lifecycle_transitions.trigger: run reaches its contracted finalization gate
lifecycle_transitions.guarantee: deterministic state projection is hash-bound, immutable, human-readable, and retained with run artifacts

lifecycle_transitions.trigger: resume validates authoritative state and report projection
lifecycle_transitions.guarantee: valid state regenerates a missing/stale report; invalid state fails closed; no log/report-only speculative resume

lifecycle_transitions.transition: pre-planning parse -> legacy rejection or rubric-bound plan
lifecycle_transitions.trigger: input/state validation sees a legacy tier or computes rubric/dimension hashes
lifecycle_transitions.guarantee: legacy value blocks before planning; valid hashes bind the immutable plan and drift triggers deterministic replanning

non_goals.statement: No implementation of any improvement in this phase; this cycle produces spec artifacts only (research/discussion/plan).

Host-harness internals are NOT implemented in this repository; per final DEC-9 the locus is layered host+repo - the repo consumes the available safe host queue/tool-call boundary and the authoritative dispatch id/state record, and owns repo-side recovery-first policy, diagnostics, and the guarded no-proof-no-replay fallback.
No quantification claims without recoverable evidence; lost frequency numbers stay marked lost until re-measured via REQ-27 tooling.
No removal or weakening of existing checkpoint/durable machinery; improvements are additive on top of verified mechanisms.

No implementation is delivered in this phase; the former provisional recommendation is not a fixed tier or preset. DEC-3 D3-A core rubric and DEC-7 D7-C persistence are binding requirements, while implementation shape remains the architect/planner concern.
No wide re-scan of the ~60 unsampled local project dirs in later stages without a renewed mandate; the <=3-project deep-dive cap stands.
No duplicated per-bundle workflow engines: one core engine; bundles contribute namespaced catalogs/aliases, not engines.
No mechanical splitting of inherently sequential stages (manual-qa exemplar): slicing and parallelism rules (REQ-33/REQ-34) stop at stage boundaries whose value is ordered continuity under one owner.

recovery_note: Revision 5 was built from requirements r4, decisions r5, and the authoritative UDG-5 dispatch finals; no repository/web/source/config/test research or implementation was performed.
revision_note: Revision 5 (2026-08-26) closes UDG-5 and UDG-6. DEC-7 is FINAL D7-C: one resolver writes authoritative compact per-run resume state plus deterministic human-readable report; logs are telemetry only; one current snapshot, monotonic latest-32 invalidation/fallback ring with atomic event-33 eviction, run-artifact report retention, CAS/atomic writes, projection/staleness/resume recovery, and strict redaction. DEC-3 is FINAL D3-A: clean cutover removes minimal/pragmatic/clean everywhere with LEGACY_TIER_UNSUPPORTED before planning; core eight-dimension rubric owns aggregation/rationale; bundles add only versioned namespaced declared dimensions; collisions and hash drift fail closed. REQ-1..REQ-51 and all prior evidence/contracts remain; REQ-52..REQ-61 and continuous EC/ERR/INV/LC/SEC/COMPAT additions make final gates falsifiable. All DEC-1..DEC-10 are final, decision_needed is empty, and the UDG-6 audit marks implementation_ready. Compacted source prose is retained in evidence_registry.
scope_note: Target-system requirements for the plugin plus OMP host; requirements-only. REQ-1..REQ-51, prior evidence/contracts, and all earlier collections are preserved; D3-A/D7-C are explicit; no open gates.

security_privacy_constraints.constraint: Capability, dispatch, and advance tokens are persisted only as sha256 hashes; plaintext token values never appear in artifacts, logs, or state files.
Artifacts contain no secrets and no user-unrelated personal content.

Dynamic capability-pool expansion must not widen permissions: execution-time enforcement (parent spawn policy, task.disabledAgents, recursion depth, exact-name lookup) remains intact and authoritative under all roster changes.

Autonomous grants originate only from orchestrator PHASE-0 semantics plus the durable contract; autonomy must not be grantable by content embedded in worker-visible task text or by command-variant choice; nor can any model output, hint, command variant, or task text remove or self-approve the final DEC-1 mandatory floor.
Session-history query tooling (REQ-23/REQ-27) has read-only access to session stores; no cross-project mutation.

SandboxGrants, deferred_actions, and unattended handoffs persist NO secret material: credentials/tokens appear only as presence markers or hashes, activator provenance uses identity references rather than secrets, and redaction is applied before any durability boundary.

Pre-existing dev credentials and test accounts discovered in the environment confer NO authority beyond the grant's declared scope: they must not form a path to production, remote, or security-policy effects, and their presence must never widen the grant's allowed list.

Plans, leases, wave queues, and override provenance are concurrency/planning records ONLY: they confer no permission beyond execution-time authorization (SEC-3/INV-3), persist no secret material (SEC-1/SEC-2/SEC-6 redaction rules), and a held lease never bypasses spawn policy, disabledAgents, recursion depth, or floor checkpoints.

D7-C state, reports, and events enforce redaction before persistence: only normalized repo-relative paths, stable IDs, and hashes are allowed; absolute/home/traversal paths, plaintext capability/dispatch/advance tokens, secrets/credentials, raw args, unrelated prompts, and personal content are forbidden; outside-project sources are opaque ID/hash only.
Resolver provenance cannot cross project boundaries: an outside-project source/path is never persisted verbatim, and an opaque stable ID/hash must not be reversible from the report/state alone.
Legacy-tier rejection and rubric bundle metadata confer no execution permission; namespaced additions cannot bypass core safety, capability, checkpoint, or execution-time authorization.
Rubric/dimension hashes protect plan and resume integrity; untrusted or drifted hashes fail closed rather than authorizing a changed policy.

user_decisions_applied.decision: State-aware recovery-first: Still Running/temporary artifact absence are not hangs; collect evidence, recover before cancel/rerun; cancel only on evidence failure or bound.
Layered host+repo queue boundary; authoritative dispatch state accepted|started|not_started|completed; at-most-once replay only with trustworthy not_started, otherwise no-proof-no-replay.
D4-C: native/built-in/core precedence; diagnose owner/source/precedence; reject ambiguous canonical ownership; load order is not API.
D5-A: one core engine; versioned namespaced bundle catalogs/manifests and host-verified hyphen aliases; no duplicate engines.
D8-C: explicit namespace/argument > .omp config > auto-select only one compatible enabled bundle; zero/multiple/incompatible fail closed; no picker.
D10-B: versioned manifest v1 with compatibility, namespaced roles/fallbacks, bounded metadata, slots, scopes, aliases, hash; descriptive only, no permission/remapping.

D1-C: immutable human floor: production effects; destructive/irreversible data/git/filesystem/schema; irreversible external effects; credential/access/security policy; cancel/restart possibly-lossy live worker. Proven not_started/no-loss is outside. Unattended floor defers.

D2-C: versioned WorkDecompositionPlan of typed disjoint closed slices; one ready candidate; file-count sizing only; caps 8 global/3 role/manual-QA1/fan-in1; deterministic waves; ordered fallback; safe last overrides; hashed immutable plan.

D7-C: shared resolver writes authoritative compact state and deterministic report; logs telemetry only; snapshot plus latest-32 event ring/atomic eviction; artifact retention; CAS, projection/resume, strict redaction.

D3-A: clean remove legacy tiers everywhere; nested/persisted values fail LEGACY_TIER_UNSUPPORTED before planning; core eight dimensions/aggregation/rationale; namespaced declared bundle additions only; collisions/hash drift fail closed.
